correctness.rationale: Rojas--Lira, Lemma 3.1 and Lemma 3.6, give an exhaustive 16+4*12 parametrization of all 64 Schur lines. For each line the proof calculates intrinsic normalized six-component Plucker coordinates and extracts exact minimal coefficient fields (not just ambient fields of some basis vectors). The field-by-family table sums to 6,2,2,34,20; exact nontrivial Galois involutions fix 8,8,40 lines, and the orbit profile is 1^6 2^19 4^5. Six rational Plucker points are enumerated, their 8 intersection edges are determined by the Klein polar form, and exhaustive graph inspection establishes maximal rational skew subset size 4. The standalone exact symbolic verifier reconstructs/independently checks all 64 lines, their inclusion, distinctness and Galois and incidence counts. Exhaustiveness beyond 64 candidate lines rests on the published geometric theorem, not on software absence-of-counterexample claims.

originality.rationale: The original 2019 paper supplies the 64-line equations and the complex maximum 16 skew lines, while the 2012 paper supplies incidence matrix and geometric chamber counts; these are premises, not novel results. Their inspected full texts do not state complete minimal-field counts, Galois orbit profile, number of real lines for this rational model or maximal rational skew subset. A published spectral/common-transversal computation treats complex graph invariants; the 2026 24-line subconfiguration over Q(sqrt(-3)) does not classify all lines. Real and published-record searches found no equivalent field census. Older Segre arithmetic literature was inaccessible, so bibliographic overlap risk remains.
residual_risks: The 2019 and 2012 line lists contain enough equations that the arithmetic table could have been calculated implicitly or in nonindexed supplements; no claim of logical independence from those formulas.
Segre 1946 arithmetical quartic paper was not read; it is a named plausible historical overlap source, so exact novelty cannot be universally certified.
The 2026 24-line paper could contain arithmetic details beyond its abstract; no unsupported whole-paper noncoverage claim is made.
This self-review is not an independent bibliography or proof audit.

value.rationale: The Schur quartic maximizes the number of lines on a smooth complex quartic; the exact minimal field of *every* line and induced 64-point arithmetic Galois action are intrinsic invariants of the fixed Q-model. Full field census (6,2,2,34,20) and sharp 4-skew rational versus known 16-skew geometric bound motivate precise arithmetic use of the configuration (e.g. permutation action on its line-generated divisor subgroup). This is a complete natural invariant/classification, not a random sample or a restatement of 64 complex lines. It does not claim the full arithmetic Picard group or any general result for every quartic surface.
